# OXCORD: High-Performance Modular Discord Library for Rust (Edition 2024)

> Official Documentation & AI Developer Context for OXCORD (`oxcord`)
> Repository: https://github.com/wumx-labs/oxcord
> Documentation Portal: https://oxcord.noxlydev.xyz
> Discord Support: https://discord.gg/JnTRems5CT
> Crates.io: https://crates.io/crates/oxcord

## Overview
OXCORD is an enterprise-grade, ultra-scalable Rust library for the Discord API, built on Rust Edition 2024 and Rust 1.85+.
It scales seamlessly from a single-process weekend bot to massive enterprise bots serving tens of thousands of guilds across distributed container clusters.

## Core Philosophy & Architecture
- **Zero Lock Contention**: State cache built on concurrent lock-free data structures.
- **Modular Architecture**: 12 independent crates (use only what you need, from pure models to distributed brokers).
- **Distributed by Design**: Native pluggable message brokers (`oxcord-broker`) supporting In-Process, NATS, Kafka, and Redis Pub/Sub.
- **Full Discord Feature Parity**: Components v2, Application Commands, Voice v4/v8, Polls, AutoMod, Onboarding, and Webhooks.

## Quick Start Example
```rust
use oxcord::prelude::*;

struct Handler;

#[async_trait]
impl EventHandler for Handler {
    async fn message(&self, ctx: Context, msg: Message) {
        if msg.content == "!ping" {
            if let Err(why) = msg.channel_id.say(&ctx.http, "Pong! 🏓").await {
                eprintln!("Error sending message: {why:?}");
            }
        }
    }
}

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() {
    let token = std::env::var("DISCORD_TOKEN").expect("DISCORD_TOKEN must be set");
    let intents = GatewayIntents::GUILD_MESSAGES | GatewayIntents::MESSAGE_CONTENT;

    let mut client = Client::builder(&token, intents)
        .event_handler(Handler)
        .await
        .expect("Error creating client");

    if let Err(why) = client.start().await {
        eprintln!("Client error: {why:?}");
    }
}
```

## Crates & API Reference
- [`oxcord`](https://docs.rs/oxcord): Unified facade crate providing high-level ergonomics, client, framework, and full re-exports
- [`oxcord-model`](https://docs.rs/oxcord-model): Complete Discord API data models, snowflakes, events, channels, messages, and permissions
- [`oxcord-builders`](https://docs.rs/oxcord-builders): Type-safe fluent request builders for messages, embeds, buttons, selects, modals, and commands
- [`oxcord-rest`](https://docs.rs/oxcord-rest): High-performance HTTP client with automated rate-limiting buckets and multipart support
- [`oxcord-gateway`](https://docs.rs/oxcord-gateway): WebSocket connection manager, heartbeat monitor, compression, and shard manager
- [`oxcord-cache`](https://docs.rs/oxcord-cache): Zero-lock-contention in-memory cache engine for guilds, channels, roles, and members
- [`oxcord-voice`](https://docs.rs/oxcord-voice): Voice gateway driver, RTP audio streaming, Opus encoder integration, and encryption
- [`oxcord-voice-model`](https://docs.rs/oxcord-voice-model): Voice gateway v4/v8 data protocol models and encryption payload structures
- [`oxcord-broker`](https://docs.rs/oxcord-broker): Distributed microservices message broker supporting In-Process, Redis Pub/Sub, Kafka, and NATS
- [`oxcord-framework`](https://docs.rs/oxcord-framework): High-level poise-equivalent unified slash + prefix command framework with cooldowns and autocomplete
- [`oxcord-macros`](https://docs.rs/oxcord-macros): Procedural macros (#[command]) for oxcord-framework declarative commands
- [`oxcord-command-attr`](https://docs.rs/oxcord-command-attr): Procedural attribute macros (`#[command]`, `#[group]`, `#[check]`) for legacy text command routing
- [`oxcord-proxy`](https://docs.rs/oxcord-proxy): Standalone reverse-proxy binary for centralized REST API Discord rate-limiting
- [`oxcord-gateway-daemon`](https://docs.rs/oxcord-gateway-daemon): Standalone daemon binary for distributed multi-server gateway sharder nodes
